clue.text: Victim is informal with heartless judge

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the word is cut out

parts.note: casual means relaxed, not formal
to try a case is to judge it in court

explanation.surface: Someone wronged by a judge who is casual and uncaring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless judge' paints an uncaring magistrate, but heartless here only removes a middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A casualty is a person killed or injured in an accident or war, hence a victim.

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the first piece goes within the second

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class
L is the standard abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: An instruction to hold a teacher back in the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: the strongest tower of a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified central tower of a medieval stronghold, and a castle is such a fortress.

clue.text: Put an end to good spirits

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stop or crush a rumour or plan
second meaning: fine whisky distilled in Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: 'Good spirits' suggests cheerfulness, but it means drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour is to stamp it out, and Scotch is the whisky made in Scotland.

clue.text: Some care naturally for The Ring

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a run of letters taken from inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Looking after Wagner's Ring cycle comes easily to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' looks like Wagner's operas; here it is the circus or boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring for boxing or the circus is an enclosed space for performance or contest, which is an arena.

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Tory
horse racing is a sport

explanation.surface: A Conservative party leader's favourite sport is chasing quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracing someone means following their trail until they are found, which is hunting them down.

indicators.note: an instrument fitted with a part has that part put inside it

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A violin is being restrung with a fresh string.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside STRAD, between its A and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a single thread or length of fibre, much like a string.

parts.note: to tip someone is to give them a small sum for service
Staffs is the short form of Staffordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A request to fund the officials of a county council.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffordshire is a county in the English Midlands, routinely shortened to Staffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipstaffs are court officers, named after the metal-tipped staff carried as a badge of their office.

clue.text: A way to keep all one's products organised

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
a firm's range is the full set of goods it sells

explanation.surface: Advice on keeping every item a business makes in order.
explanation.walkthrough: A way is a road, and crosswords use the street-sign abbreviation for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged has been put into a planned order, just as organised things have.

indicators.note: fancy describes something elaborate or made up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man named Ed disliked a flashy necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie' looks like neckwear, but it is a drawn race.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race in which two competitors finish level, which is a tie.

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed and stirred up, so its letters are mixed

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An employee is upset at having no boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A storeman is an employee who looks after a warehouse or stockroom, so a type of worker.

clue.text: Creative work found in resort in ancient Greece

definitions.note: a place phrase rather than a noun: Sparta was a city state there

indicators.note: a thing found in a place is located within it, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a spa is a resort with mineral springs
art is creative work

explanation.surface: A painting discovered at a holiday town in classical Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a city that existed in ancient Greece, so the phrase names where it was rather than what it was.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was the warlike city state of the Peloponnese, a leading power of classical Greek history.

indicators.note: the first piece is placed in the second, sitting inside it

parts.note: to venture money is to wager it
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A chivalrous knight caught up in a crooked enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: N is used for knight in chess because K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is British slang for corrupt, especially of police or officials, so it means dishonest.

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A drug company produced an essential remedy that earns money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucrative business brings in a great deal of money, so it is highly profitable.

clue.text: Fish smell loses its initial character

indicators.note: losing the initial character means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a stench is a foul smell

explanation.surface: A fishy odour is fading away.
explanation.walkthrough: STENCH drops its opening S.
explanation.definitionFit: The tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family, found in European ponds and rivers.

parts.note: a bob was a shilling, abbreviated S
a stein is a large beer mug

explanation.surface: A man called Bob Stein is vain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob Stein' reads as a person's name. A bob is slang for a shilling, an old British coin, written S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smug is self-satisfied and pleased with themselves, which is a form of conceit.

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving with the navy
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A soldier eating a fish feast laid out before him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb describing a meal laid out; it is the noun for what goes on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute that people put on bread, so it is a spread.

indicators.note: to reject something is to turn it back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: oily and fat both describe greasy food
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: Turning down a greasy cheesecloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheese cloth' suggests the muslin used in dairies, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven fabric of silk or synthetic fibre, so a type of cloth.

indicators.note: one thing set round another surrounds it on both sides

parts.note: a camera pans when it sweeps across a scene
a gun barrel is a pipe

explanation.surface: A device that examines the curve of a cask.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrel here is a gun barrel, a tube, not a cask; a film camera that sweeps sideways is said to pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Panpipes are a wind instrument made of a row of reeds of different lengths bound together.

clue.text: Peter to rearrange a musical work

indicators.note: to rearrange is to put things in a different order

parts.note: letters to rearrange
taken as written and added to the mix

explanation.surface: Peter is asked to arrange a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal sits between its fodder words, which is easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a short light opera with spoken dialogue, a kind of musical work.

parts.note: aspiring means eagerly desiring, and the apostrophe shows the final G clipped

explanation.surface: Someone longing for a drug, said in a casual drawl.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in desirin' is the signal: drop the G of aspiring in the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling medicine, acetylsalicylic acid, so it is a drug.

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the sound is what counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to know of something is to be aware of it

explanation.surface: Someone notices a strong odour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced smell' reads as a strong smell, but pronounced is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to nose is to smell or sniff something out, and a nose is the sense of smell.

clue.text: US president gets transport to hotel

parts.note: a bus is public transport
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A president is given a ride to his hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Two American presidents, father and son George Bush, held the office from the White House.

parts.note: the bar is the rail in a courtroom, and the legal profession
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: A violent attack provokes fury in a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assault' sounds like a criminal charge in the court, but it is a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a heavy bombardment of artillery fire, a sustained military attack.

parts.note: a dry talk is dull and boring
a spell of something, as in a run of luck

explanation.surface: A dull stretch during a play's practice session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' could mean drilling a hole; here it means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry run is a practice attempt before the real thing, which is what a rehearsal is.

clue.text: Fellow salesman's up for a drink

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means reading from the bottom, so the order is backwards

parts.note: a don is a fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A colleague in sales is ready for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': fellow and salesman together is up. DON REP read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is a French aniseed-flavoured aperitif, an alcoholic drink.

parts.note: to park is to leave a car somewhere
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone leaves their car, taking a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof coat, so it is a type of jacket.

indicators.note: what is swallowed goes inside, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a surge is a heaving swell of the sea
char is a fish of the trout family

explanation.surface: Someone retches on swallowing a fish oil capsule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heave' suggests retching, but it is the swell of the sea; 'supplement' suggests a vitamin pill, but it is an extra charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A surcharge is an extra charge added on top of a price, a supplement to the bill.

parts.note: to have had to put up with something is to tolerate it
in bridge, East and South are opposing seats

explanation.surface: The dog Pluto put up with rival card players.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto suggests the cartoon dog or the dwarf planet, but it is the Roman god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto is the Roman name of the Greek god Hades, ruler of the underworld.

parts.note: to set something down is to put it there
to rid is to free or clear

explanation.surface: Someone spun round and was released from captivity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set free' reads as one phrase meaning released; split it into two words. 'Turned' means gone off, as milk turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has turned has gone sour or rotten, and putrid means decaying and foul.

clue.text: Bureaucrat with a right to enter ministry

indicators.note: pieces that enter something go inside it

parts.note: MIN is the abbreviation for ministry
and means with or plus
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An official with a right of entry into a government department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is not a link here: it supplies its own synonym, which goes in along with the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin is a powerful senior civil servant, named after officials of imperial China.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: went up a wall or mountain
second meaning: covered in scales, as a snake's skin is

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests climbing with a slithering motion; the second half is about the snake's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a cliff is to climb it, and a snake's body is covered in scales.

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its order or form

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Rational people are bold enough to accept change.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoned argument is built through careful step-by-step thought, so it is logical.
